REMOTE_DIR="${FTP_REMOTE_DIR:?Set FTP_REMOTE_DIR (e.g. /public_html)}"

HOST="${FTP_HOST:-ftps4.us.freehostia.com}"
USER_NAME="${FTP_USER:-aksgul5}"
REMOTE_DIR="${FTP_REMOTE_DIR:?Set FTP_REMOTE_DIR (e.g. /public_html)}"

DELETE=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --apply) APPLY=1 ;;
    --delete) DELETE=1 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown arg: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

command -v lftp >/dev/null || { echo "lftp missing: brew install lftp" >&2; exit 1; }

# --- Branch guard -----------------------------------------------------------
BRANCH="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ] && [ "$BRANCH" != "main" ]; then
  echo "WARNING: on branch '$BRANCH', not master/main."
  echo "         The deployed site will be built from this branch."
  ans=""
  read -r -p "Continue anyway? [y/N] " ans || true
  case "$ans" in
    y|Y|yes|YES) ;;
    *) echo "Aborted."; exit 1 ;;
  esac
fi

# --- Temp files -------------------------------------------------------------
BUILD_LOG="$(mktemp)"
ACTIONS="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$BUILD_LOG" "$ACTIONS"' EXIT

# --- Live status line -------------------------------------------------------
if [ -t 1 ]; then
  TTY=1
  COLS="$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 80)"
else
  TTY=0
  COLS=80
fi

# status "text": rewrite the current line (or plain line when not a TTY)
status() {
  if [ "$TTY" -eq 1 ]; then
    local s="$1"
    [ "${#s}" -ge "$COLS" ] && s="${s:0:$((COLS - 2))}…"
    printf '\r\033[K%s' "$s"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$1"
  fi
}

if ! npm run build >"$BUILD_LOG" 2>&1; then
  endstatus
  echo "Build failed:" >&2
  tail -n 40 "$BUILD_LOG" >&2
  exit 1
fi
endstatus

[ -f dist/index.html ] || { echo "dist/index.html missing, aborting" >&2; exit 1; }

  PASS="$(security find-generic-password -a "$USER_NAME" -s jcc-ftp -w 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [ -z "$PASS" ]; then
  read -r -s -p "FTP password for $USER_NAME@$HOST: " PASS
  echo

[ "$DELETE" -eq 1 ] && OPTS="$OPTS --delete"
if [ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ]; then
  OPTS="$OPTS --dry-run"
  echo "DRY RUN (use --apply to upload)"
fi

# --- Run lftp, parse its output into live status + action list --------------
# Script goes via stdin, so the password never appears in argv / ps.
# lftp verbose lines parsed:
#   Transferring file `X'      -> upload X
#   Removing old file `X'      -> remove X (before overwrite, or --delete)
#   Making directory `X'       -> mkdir X
#   Removing old directory `X' -> rmdir X
set +e
lftp <<EOF 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do
set cmd:fail-exit yes
set ftp:ssl-force true
set ftp:ssl-protect-data true
set ftp:ssl-protect-list true
set ftp:ssl-allow no
set ssl:verify-certificate yes
set net:max-retries 2
set net:timeout 20
status "Connecting to $HOST..."
open -u "$USER_NAME","$PASS" ftp://$HOST
mirror $OPTS --exclude-glob .DS_Store dist/ "$REMOTE_DIR"
bye

  case "$line" in
    "Transferring file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'T\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "$([ "$APPLY" -eq 1 ] && echo Uploading || echo Checking): $f" ;;
    "Removing old file \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'R\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Replacing: $f" ;;
    "Making directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'M\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Creating dir: $f" ;;
    "Removing old directory \`"*)
      f="${line#*\`}"; f="${f%\'}"
      printf 'X\t%s\n' "$f" >>"$ACTIONS"
      status "Removing dir: $f" ;;
    # dry-run echoes the underlying commands; ignore that noise
    "get "*|"put "*|"rm "*|"rmdir "*|"mkdir "*|"") ;;
    *)
      endstatus
      printf '%s\n' "$line" >&2 ;;
  esac
done
RC="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
set -e
endstatus

if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "lftp failed (exit $RC). Check output above." >&2
  exit "$RC"
fi

# --- Summary ----------------------------------------------------------------
# A file with both R and T = overwritten; T only = new; R only = deleted.
awk -F'\t' -v apply="$APPLY" '
  $1=="T" { t[$2]=1; order[++n]=$2 }
  $1=="R" { r[$2]=1; if (!($2 in seen)) { seen[$2]=1; rorder[++m]=$2 } }
  $1=="M" { dirs[++d]=$2 }
  $1=="X" { rdirs[++x]=$2 }
  END {
    for (i=1;i<=n;i++) { f=order[i]; if (f in r) upd[++u]=f; else new[++w]=f }
    for (i=1;i<=m;i++) { f=rorder[i]; if (!(f in t)) del[++k]=f }
    verb = apply ? "Changed" : "Would change"
    print ""
    print "== " verb ": " u+0 " updated, " w+0 " new, " k+0 " deleted, " d+0 " dirs created, " x+0 " dirs removed =="
    cap=100
    sec("Updated", upd, u, cap, "~")
    sec("New", new, w, cap, "+")
    sec("Deleted", del, k, cap, "-")
    sec("Dirs created", dirs, d, cap, "+")
    sec("Dirs removed", rdirs, x, cap, "-")
    if (u+w+k+d+x == 0) print "Nothing to do: remote already up to date."
  }
  function sec(title, arr, cnt, cap, mark,   i) {
    if (cnt+0 == 0) return
    print title " (" cnt "):"
    for (i=1;i<=cnt && i<=cap;i++) print "  " mark " " arr[i]
    if (cnt > cap) print "  ... and " (cnt-cap) " more"
  }
' "$ACTIONS"

[ "$APPLY" -eq 0 ] && echo && echo "Dry run only. Re-run with --apply to upload."
exit 0

Usage: python3 -I fakeftp.py PORT

import socket
import sys

port = int(sys.argv[1])
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
srv.listen(4)
srv.settimeout(12)

for _ in range(3):
    try:
        conn, _addr = srv.accept()
    except socket.timeout:
        break
    conn.settimeout(8)
    f = conn.makefile("rwb")

    def send(x):
        f.write(x.encode() + b"\r\n")
        f.flush()

    print("--- new connection", flush=True)
    send("220 fake ftp")
    try:
        while True:
            line = f.readline()
            if not line:
                break
            cmd = line.decode(errors="replace").strip()
            print("C:", cmd, flush=True)
            verb = cmd.split(" ")[0].upper()
            if verb == "FEAT":

                send("530 login incorrect")
            elif verb == "QUIT":
                send("221 bye")
                break

                send("502 not implemented")

        pass
    conn.close()

  * With `ftp:ssl-allow yes`, lftp sent `AUTH TLS`. When the server refused, it stopped with `ftp:ssl-force is set and server does not support or allow SSL`, before sending the username or password.
  * An unmodified copy of the script, run end to end, also sent `USER aksgul5` and `PASS <pw>` with no encryption.
  * With `--parallel=2`, every extra connection sends the password again.
* **Exploit scenario:** Anyone on the network path can read the password as it goes past: public Wi-Fi, a compromised router, the ISP, or the host's own network.   ```
  set ftp:ssl-allow yes
  set ftp:ssl-force yes
  set ftp:ssl-auth TLS
  set ftp:ssl-protect-data yes
  set ftp:ssl-protect-list yes
  set ssl:verify-certificate yes

## Below the confidence bar (7/10, not reported as a finding)

**The default dry run prints the password to the terminal** (`deploy-ftp.sh:129`, `:151`, `:154`). I tested this end to end; I'm listing it because the fix is small and the exposure is real.
* `mirror --dry-run` prints lines such as `chmod -f 644 ftp://aksgul5:<password>@host/...`.
* The output filter on line 151 doesn't drop `chmod` lines, so line 154 prints them unchanged.
* Every build gives every file a new timestamp, so every dry run prints these lines.
* The repo's Entire pre-push hook pushes AI session transcripts to `origin`, and the repo is public. If the dry run is ever run through an agent's shell tool, the password could end up published. No real password has leaked so far.

The fix:
1. Use `open --env-password -u "$USER_NAME" ftp://$HOST` and run lftp as `LFTP_PASSWORD="$PASS" lftp ...`. The dry-run lines then show no password. This also keeps the password out of the lftp command text, so a `"` in it can no longer break the quoting or inject lftp commands.
2. Add `"chmod "*` to the filter on line 151.

---

## If the FTP password is compromised: impact and mitigations

**What an attacker gets.** Full write and delete access to the site's folder on Freehostia. This matters only if the domain's DNS actually points at Freehostia; CLAUDE.md says the site is on Netlify. With that access they can:
* Change payment or contact details in pages and PDFs (fees, expense form, by-laws, signed letters) to phish members on a domain they trust.
* Inject scripts for card skimming, redirects or spam, which can get the domain blocklisted by browsers.
* Probably upload a PHP webshell, since Freehostia shared hosting normally runs PHP. I have not verified this for your plan. That would give code execution as the hosting account.

**Redeploying won't clean it up.** By default the script only uploads files that are newer and never deletes anything (`--only-newer`, no `--delete`). So an attacker's added files survive every normal deploy, such as a webshell, a phishing page or an `.htaccess` redirect. A tampered file with a future timestamp is also skipped.

**Possible account takeover.** `aksgul5` looks like the main hosting login. If the same password opens the Freehostia control panel, an attacker could also take over DNS, mail and the domain itself.

**Mitigations:**
1. Fix Vuln 1, and the dry-run leak above, before the next run.
2. Use a dedicated FTP sub-account limited to the web folder, with a unique password.
3. If any version without the `ssl:min-protocol` line has ever reached the real host, change the password.
4. After a suspected compromise:
   * Change the password.
   * Check `.htaccess`, hidden files, and anything outside the web folder.
   * Do a full re-upload with `--apply --delete` and without `--only-newer`.
5. Every so often, run a `--delete` dry run to spot remote files that aren't in `dist/`.

**Hardening notes (not findings):**
* **Keychain item readable by any of your processes.** The setup command creates the item without `-T`, so any process running as you can read it without a prompt. Recreate it with `-T ""` so every read asks first.
* **`FTP_PASS` passed to the build.** If set, it is inherited by `npm run build` and every build process. Clear it before the build runs.
* **Netlify headers skipped.** A Freehostia deploy doesn't get the security headers or redirects in `netlify.toml`.
* **A passing dry run doesn't prove login or TLS worked.** It can show a plan even when the login failed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Offline regression test for scripts/deploy-ftp.sh security guarantees.
# Runs the real deploy script against a local fake FTP server (no network,
# no real credentials) and asserts that the password is never sent or printed:
#
#   1. Server without TLS          -> script aborts, server never sees USER/PASS
#   2. Server with untrusted cert  -> script aborts, server never sees USER/PASS
#
# Usage: scripts/test-deploy-ftp.sh      (needs python3, lftp, openssl, dist/)
set -uo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

[ -f dist/index.html ] || { echo "Run 'npm run build' once first (dist/ missing)." >&2; exit 2; }
for bin in python3 lftp openssl; do
  command -v "$bin" >/dev/null || { echo "Missing: $bin" >&2; exit 2; }
done

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
SRV_PID=""
cleanup() { [ -n "$SRV_PID" ] && kill "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$WORK"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

FAKE_PW="REDACTED"   # fake value; must never show up anywhere

# Stub npm so the test does not rebuild the site.
mkdir -p "$WORK/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' >"$WORK/bin/npm"
chmod +x "$WORK/bin/npm"

# Self-signed cert for test 2 (not trusted by the system CA store).
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj "/CN=127.0.0.1" \
  -keyout "$WORK/key.pem" -out "$WORK/cert.pem" >/dev/null 2>&1

cat >"$WORK/fakeftp.py" <<'PY'
import socket, ssl, sys
mode, portfile, logfile, certdir = sys.argv[1:5]
log = open(logfile, "a", buffering=1)
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
srv.listen(4)
srv.settimeout(20)
open(portfile, "w").write(str(srv.getsockname()[1]))
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
ctx.load_cert_chain(certdir + "/cert.pem", certdir + "/key.pem")
while True:
    try:
        conn, _ = srv.accept()
    except socket.timeout:
        break
    conn.settimeout(10)
    f = conn.makefile("rwb", buffering=0)
    send = lambda s: f.write((s + "\r\n").encode())
    send("220 fake")
    try:
        while True:
            line = f.readline()
            if not line:
                break
            cmd = line.decode(errors="replace").strip()
            log.write("C: " + cmd + "\n")
            verb = cmd.split(" ")[0].upper()
            if verb == "FEAT":
                f.write(b"211-Features:\r\n AUTH TLS\r\n PBSZ\r\n PROT\r\n211 End\r\n")
            elif verb == "AUTH" and mode == "notls":
                send("534 TLS refused")
            elif verb == "AUTH" and mode == "selfsigned":
                send("234 go ahead")
                try:
                    conn = ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
                    f = conn.makefile("rwb", buffering=0)
                    send = lambda s: f.write((s + "\r\n").encode())
                    log.write("TLS handshake completed\n")
                except Exception as e:
                    log.write("TLS handshake rejected by client: %s\n" % e)
                    break
            elif verb == "USER":
                send("331 need password")
            elif verb == "PASS":
                send("530 login incorrect")
            elif verb == "QUIT":
                send("221 bye")
                break
            else:
                send("502 not implemented")
    except Exception:
        pass
    conn.close()
PY

FAILS=0
check() { # check "description" condition-exit-code
  if [ "$2" -eq 0 ]; then echo "  PASS  $1"; else echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); fi
}

run_case() { # run_case mode title
  local mode="$1" title="$2"
  local portfile="$WORK/port.$mode" srvlog="$WORK/srv.$mode.log" out="$WORK/out.$mode.log"
  : >"$srvlog"
  python3 -I "$WORK/fakeftp.py" "$mode" "$portfile" "$srvlog" "$WORK" &
  SRV_PID=$!
  for _ in $(seq 50); do [ -s "$portfile" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
  local port; port="$(cat "$portfile")"

  echo "== $title"
  # "y" answers the branch guard if not on master/main.
  echo y | PATH="$WORK/bin:$PATH" FTP_HOST="127.0.0.1:$port" FTP_USER=testuser \
    FTP_PASS="$FAKE_PW" FTP_REMOTE_DIR=/www scripts/deploy-ftp.sh >"$out" 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  kill "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$SRV_PID" 2>/dev/null; SRV_PID=""

  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ];                                  check "deploy script exits non-zero (rc=$rc)" $?

  ! grep -qE '^C: (USER|PASS)' "$srvlog";           check "server never received USER/PASS" $?
  ! grep -qF "$FAKE_PW" "$srvlog" "$out";           check "password not in server log or script output" $?
  if [ "$FAILS" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "  --- server log:";  sed 's/^/    /' "$srvlog"
    echo "  --- script output:"; sed 's/^/    /' "$out"
  fi
}

run_case notls      "Server refuses TLS"
run_case selfsigned "Server presents an untrusted certificate"

# Plain FTP is refused: TLS is forced on both the control and data channels.
#
# Usage: npm run deploy:ftps [-- --dry-run] [-- --delete] [-- --skip-build]
#   --dry-run     show what would change, upload nothing

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
DRY_RUN=0; DELETE=0; BUILD=1
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;

command -v lftp >/dev/null || { echo "lftp not found. Install it: brew install lftp" >&2; exit 1; }
ENV_FILE=".env.deploy"
[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || { echo "Missing $ENV_FILE (copy .env.deploy.example)" >&2; exit 1; }
# Refuse a config file other users can read.
if [ -n "$(find "$ENV_FILE" -perm -044 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
